en: The Mahāvaipulya Dhāraṇī Sūtra, Part One, Scroll One.
Translated by the Śramaṇa Fa-zhong of the Northern Liang during the Gaochang Commandery.
Part One: Thus have I heard. At one time the Buddha was staying in the Jeta Grove in the kingdom of Śrāvastī, together with five...
Accompanied by the one hundred great disciples,
at that time Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta departed from the city of Rājagṛha together with a multitude of ninety-two billion bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Their names were the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī,
the Dharma Prince Maitreyarāja,
the Dharma Prince Mahāmaudgalyāyana, and the Dharma Prince Brahmaghoṣa.
The Dharma Prince Sublime Form, the Dharma Prince Sandalwood Forest,
the Dharma Prince Lion’s Roar Sound,
and the Dharma Prince Sublime Voice.
The Dharma Prince of Wondrous Form and Appearance,
the Dharma Prince of Various Ornaments,
the Dharma Prince Śakradhvaja, and the Dharma Prince Mūrdhaja.
In this manner, ninety-two billion [beings] arrived at the Jeta Grove and beheld the Buddha, the World-Honored One.
They circumambulated the Buddha three times, prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet, and then withdrew to stand to one side.
He exhorted the World-Honored One to turn the wheel of Dharma.
Great King Prasenajit, accompanied by five hundred princes—
among them Prince Ghaṇṭila and Prince Jīvaka— [approached him].
The prince Satyarūpa, the prince Dharmarūpa,
and these five hundred princes likewise went to the Jeta Grove,
circumambulated the Buddha three times, and stood before him.
Having prostrated with his head at the Blessed One’s feet,
he stood to one side and exhorted the Blessed One to turn the wheel of Dharma.
This was the upāsaka Ugga of Haṅkha in the city of Śrāvastī.
He was accompanied by six hundred upāsakas,
namely: the upāsaka Ugata, the upāsaka Susvara, the upāsaka Lakṣaṇālaṃkṛta, and the upāsaka Cittaśobhana.
The upāsaka Sudatta and these six hundred other upāsakas went to Jeta’s Grove,
circumambulated the Buddha three times, and stood to one side.
They prostrated with their heads at his feet and stood to one side,
entreating the World-Honored One to turn the wheel of the Dharma.
There were also five hundred devout upāsikās.
Their names were the female lay follower Viśākhā, the female lay follower Śūnyatālakṣaṇā,
the female lay follower Puṣpadattā, and the female lay follower Kṣāntivādī.
The upāsikā Cāndrā and the upāsikā Mahāprajāpatī—
these five hundred upāsikās and others went to the Jeta Grove,
circumambulated the Buddha three times, and stood to one side.
Having prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, he stood to one side.
He then entreated the World-Honored One to turn the wheel of Dharma. Furthermore, there was the householder’s son Ugga together with five hundred other sons of householders.
Their names were the elder’s son Sudatta, the elder’s son Virūḍhaka,
the elder’s son Candanavana, and the elder’s son Surūpa.
These five hundred sons of elders,
having arrived at the Jeta Grove, circumambulated the Buddha three times,
prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet, and withdrew to stand to one side.
He exhorted the World-Honored One to turn the wheel of Dharma.
At that time, Mañjuśrī rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, and—
Placing his right knee upon the ground, he joined his palms in reverence and,
without averting his gaze for a moment, addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One, Tathāgata, regarding all the various dharanī gateways that you have previously and subsequently taught."
He is the most supreme among all the worlds;
he is the most supreme within the True Dharma;
and he is the most supreme among all the devas.
Sentient beings enter the gates of various dhāraṇīs and contemplate the realm of the Buddha by means of this most supreme Dharma.
Out of the power of compassion, the World-Honored One acts for the sake of immeasurable and boundless sentient beings.
He expounded and explained the names of the dhāraṇīs.
The Buddha said to Mañjuśrī,
“Excellent, excellent, son of good family!”
For the sake of sentient beings who undergo immeasurable suffering and affliction,
you have inquired about the gateway of dhāraṇī.
Good son, listen now with close attention.
I shall briefly explain for you the names of the various dhāraṇīs.
Son of good family,
there is a dhāraṇī named Mahā-tantrī.
There is a dhāraṇī named Mahālipati; there is a dhāraṇī named Ratnaketu;
there is a dhāraṇī named Ratnārcis.
There is a dhāraṇī named Ratnacchattra;
there is a dhāraṇī named Vajracchattra;
and there is a dhāraṇī named Vajraraśmi.
There is a dhāraṇī named Adornment of All Colors;
there is a dhāraṇī named Vajra Body;
there is a dhāraṇī named Heavy Adornment.
There is a dhāraṇī named Bahudhāra; there is a dhāraṇī named Vigatadhāra;
there is a dhāraṇī named Jalaprabhā.
There is a dhāraṇī named Samādhi;
there is a dhāraṇī named Flower-Cluster;
there is a dhāraṇī named Determination.
There is a dhāraṇī named Constant Abiding;
there is a dhāraṇī named Multitude of Flower Fragrances;
there is a dhāraṇī named Various Radiances.
Good son, for each of these dhāraṇīs,
there are ninety-two billion monks as numerous as the sands of the Ganges;
furthermore, for each individual dhāraṇī, there are again ninety-two billion monks as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
The wise one should explain this in three sections in successive order.
When these names of the various dhāraṇīs were being spoken,
ninety-two billion bodhisattvas led by Mañjuśrī dwelt in the patience of the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
Six hundred upāsakas dwelt in the mind of a pratyekabuddha;
five hundred upāsikās were distanced from dust and free from defilement, attaining the purity of the Dharma-eye;
and five hundred sons of elders gave rise to the mind of *samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The various princes led by King Prasenajit requested ordination before the Tathāgata.
The Buddha said to the princes, "Excellent, excellent!"
"You may now rightly seek ordination within my Dharma; this is precisely the time.
The Buddha said to the princes, "Welcome, bhikṣus!
At that moment, the hair and beards of the princes fell away of their own accord, and the dharma robes were donned upon their bodies.
He immediately became a śramaṇa, fully endowed with the practice of the precepts.
At that time, the World-Honored One expounded the Dharma of the Four Noble Truths for the bhikṣus.
Then, the bhikṣus became fully possessed of the three types of clear knowledge (trividyā) and the six supernormal powers (ṣaḍabhijñā).
At that time, the bhikṣus exhorted the World-Honored One to turn the wheel of Dharma.
Thereupon, the World-Honored One signaled his assent by remaining silent;
he then entered the gates of various dhāraṇīs and emitted a great radiance.
It illuminated immeasurable billions of nayutas of trichiliocosms in the eastern direction, behind Mount Yugandhara;
having emitted this light, there were immeasurable billions of nayutas of yakṣas.
In the south, west, north, and the four intermediate directions;
from below, as far as the Kāṭanarāja heaven, to above, reaching up to the realm of consciousness—
the worlds of the ten directions are likewise thus.
Each had immeasurable billions of nayutas of yakṣa hosts;
having beheld this light,
they immediately followed its radiance and came to the Sahā world.
Arriving at the Jeta Grove,
he saw the Tathāgata Śākyamuni entering the gates of various dhāraṇīs,
and he also saw the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī standing to the left and right of the Buddha.
They wished to request the World-Honored One to turn the wheel of Dharma.
At that time, there was a multitude of immeasurable billions of nayutas of yakṣas,
as well as Mañjuśrī and the various bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.
Together with five hundred great disciples— monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, and the sons of householders—
each entered various *dhāraṇī* gates following the Buddha.
At that time, there was a monk in the assembly named Ghoṣadatta (Thunder Voice).
He immediately rose from his seat, went into the forest, and entered into meditative absorption (*dhyāna-samādhi*).
At that time, there was a host of Māras in the sky. Among them was a Māra king named Caṇḍāla.
In the midst of the void, he formed this thought:
"The Buddha Śākyamuni of former times was surrounded before and behind by an immeasurable great assembly."
I have preached the Dharma for them, enabling them to obtain great and wholesome benefit.
Now this bhikṣu has again entered the samādhi of meditative concentration;
if I do not sever the causal conditions of this bhikṣu’s roots of goodness, [he will fall into evil destinies].
This bhikṣu will surely, within this Bhadrakalpa,
attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment;
he shall achieve omniscience and obtain great, wholesome benefit.
"I shall now, together with my retinue,
destroy the causes and conditions for that bhikṣu’s roots of goodness.
At that time, Māra the King immediately took ninety-two billion followers with him.
He went to the Jeta Grove and concealed the causes and conditions of this bhikṣu’s roots of goodness.
At that time, the bhikṣu Ghoṣadatta...
Filled with profound grief and sorrow, he cried out in a loud voice:
"Homage to the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions and three periods of time!
Homage to the immeasurable Dharmas of the ten directions and three periods of time!"
"Homage to those who possess even a small portion of the feet [of the Buddhas] throughout the ten directions.
Having thus proclaimed,
at that time, all the Buddhas of the ten directions spoke with one voice, saying:
"With what dharma should I save those bhikṣus?
At that time, the Buddha Ratnarāja raised his hand and said,
"Among this assembly of bodhisattvas, is there perhaps any bodhisattva [who can do so]?"
"Can you save that bhikṣu from his suffering?
At that time, there was a bodhisattva in the assembly named Puṣpaketu,
who rose from his seat and bared his right shoulder.
Placing his right knee on the ground and joining his palms toward the Buddha, he addressed the Buddha, saying: "By what dharma should he be instructed regarding that Caṇḍāla?
At that time, the Buddha spoke to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Puṣpakūṭa.
"Do you not know? I have commanded that Caṇḍāla by means of the secret dharmas of all Buddhas.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Puṣpakūṭa:
"I shall [employ] the dharani-phrase of the Mahācaṇḍī."
"By subduing this Pāpīyān, he increases the roots of goodness of that bhikṣu.
Listen attentively now, for I shall explain to you the secret Dharma of all Buddhas.
Puṣpadanta addressed the Buddha, saying, "So be it, World-Honored One; we wish and desire to hear such a sublime Dharma."
The Buddha told Huajù: "I now speak to you:
do not falsely propagate such a sublime Dharma.
You should take the divine spirits as your witness."
For what reason is he called a "divine being"?
Son of good family, there shall be twelve dream-kings;
only when one sees such a king may you explain [the dream] to him.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these dhāraṇī verses:
Namo uruḍeśye tidhyakini nāgayamī svāhā. Tadyathā: pūjipriya upatavye pūjipriya lepara anutadadhā anutadadhā budagudze pūjipriya svāhā. When this dharma was spoken, [the earth trembled].
There were eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas dwelling on the stage of the "feet of a small portion.
There were two hundred and sixty thousand bhikṣus dwelling on the stage of pratyekabuddhas.
Furthermore, there were thirty-four thousand bhikṣuṇīs who had attained the fruit of arhatship.
Seventy thousand laymen (*upāsaka*) resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Five hundred laywomen (*upāsikā*) were distanced from dust and free from defilement, attaining the purity of the Dharma-eye (*dharma-cakṣur-viśuddhi*).
At that time, the Bodhisattva Puṣpasaṃcaya praised the Buddha, saying:
"The World-Honored One’s body and color are like a mountain of gold;
Like the light of the sun, he illuminates the world, Able to uproot all suffering and affliction. I now prostrate before the Great Dharma King."
The physical marks of the World-Honored One are like a great mountain; With immeasurable great compassion, he protects all beings.
We receive his teachings and shall achieve the wisdom of all modes; Having eliminated stinginess and greed, we leave behind all attachments.
The Lord of the World, King of Dharma, is most rare and marvelous; This wondrous Dharma surpasses even this.
Hard to see, hard to hear, and difficult to encounter— Whoever beholds it shall attain Perfect Enlightenment.
The World-Honored One’s power of Dharma is the mightiest of all powers; Transcending the three realms, he beholds all sentient beings.
If there are sentient beings who listen with a sincere heart, There is not a single person among them who does not attain the Way.
Since it is said that the enlightened one attains perfect awakening, delivers all sentient beings without limit,
and alone reaches the site of enlightenment to become a Teacher of Gods, he subsequently preaches the Dharma for ultimate bliss—
at this time, the Bodhisattva Flower-Cluster...
Having thus praised the Buddha, he suddenly vanished.
He then proceeded to the Sahā world in the western direction and arrived at the Jeta Grove,
where he saw the bhikṣu Thunder-Voice being obscured by ninety-two billion Māras, the sons of Pāpīyān.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Puṣpaketu said to Caṇḍāla, "Why do you now wish to destroy the causes and conditions for the roots of goodness of this bhikṣu?
The power of the World-Honored One is truly immeasurable; he is able to defeat all those of the external paths."
Able to destroy all evil thieves and able to establish all wholesome dharmas.
At that time, having heard these words, the Māra King was seized with great terror;
his heart was startled and his hair stood on end.
He immediately replied, saying:

"I am the King of the World; I possess mastery over the world and am able to destroy all [obstacles]. O you of virtuous wisdom! At that time, the Bodhisattva Puṣpaketu replied to the Māra king, saying:
“The World-Honored One’s wisdom is like space, capable of covering all evil dharmas.
I shall subdue you as one subdues a *bimba* fruit; if you do not believe me, you shall know it now.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Flower-Cluster spoke to Thunder-Sound:
Listen well now, for I shall explain to you how to subdue all evil destinies.
I shall subdue this Pāpīyān;
through this, you shall now realize and know the skillful means of all Buddhas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Puṣpaketu spoke these dhāraṇī verses:
*Namo gurgur-dheṣya | kṛti-ikṣiṇa | nāgayamī | svāhā.* When this teaching was spoken, there were six hundred māra kings.
They prostrated at the Bodhisattva’s feet, joined their palms in reverence, and addressed the Bodhisattva, saying: “There is a dhāraṇī called ‘The Self-Vow.
We wish to establish this dhāraṇī; we only pray that you will grant us your permission.”
Puṣpaka said, "Wait a moment; the time for Mañjuśrī to speak has not yet arrived.
At that time, Puṣpaka further spoke this dhāraṇī: Tadyathā:

(1) puṅgi-bimba, (2) udbhavaya, (3) puṅgi-bimba, (4) lepara, (5) anutātadyathā, (6) anutātadyathā, (7) punar-dakṣu-trai, (8) puṅgi-bimba, (9) svāhā. (10) When this Dharma was being spoken, there were six million Māras, the Pāpīyans.
"Crying out together from the same pit—how bitter this suffering is!
Since one undergoes such suffering, how can one escape it?
At that time, Puṣpasaṃcaya addressed the Māra king, saying:
"If you wish to be free from such suffering,
you may resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. "Very well,
Great Being," they replied, "we shall resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."
"Puṣpaketu said, 'Excellent, excellent! At that time, the various Māra kings spoke this dhāraṇī:

1. Namaḥ mahā-buddha-pai 2. Namaḥ mahā-ripa-buddha-pai 3. Namaḥ puṣpaketu-dhāraṇyai 4. Piśāca śmuk 5. Ugavane 6. Taṇḍavane 7. Kuṅgavane 8. Gaṅgā-gami 9. Āre 10. Nāre 11. Narāre 12. Svāhā Then Puṣpaketu praised the Māra king, saying:"
Excellent, excellent, Son of the Buddha!
That you are able to receive and uphold the phrases of the Mahādhāraṇī will bring great benefit to immeasurable hosts of Māras.
At that time, the Māra King was filled with joy and leaped for gladness;
he immediately removed the karpāsa garments from his body to offer as an act of worship.
At that moment, the accumulated garments were like Mount Sumeru in height.
They used them to make offerings to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Puṣpaketu.
Having made the offerings, they further addressed Puṣpaketu:
"We twelve great kings..."
One should uphold these verses of the Mahāpratisarā Dhāraṇī, and furthermore,
one should abundantly provide offerings to those who uphold this sūtra.
If such persons encounter suffering or calamity, [they shall be delivered].
"You should invoke my names as the Twelve Divine Kings.
At that time, Puṣpaketu addressed the Māra king,
saying, "What are their names?"
The Mara King said: "The king is named Tandra; the king is named Kṣitira;
the king is named Mucilinda; the king is named Gāndhāra;
the king is named Bahula; the king is named Pālinda."
The king was named Dānavana; the king was named Candravana.
The king was named Gaṅgavana; the king was named Kalavana.
The king was named Gaṅgavana; the king was named Palavana.
Each of these kings proclaimed: "We shall uphold,
maintain, read, and recite this dhāraṇī sūtra to protect and deliver practitioners,
causing them to strengthen their resolve for supreme enlightenment (samyak-saṃbodhi-citta) and to attain excellent benefits."
At that time, Puṣpaketu praised the Māra kings, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! On this day you have displayed great valor;
you are able to receive, uphold, and protect this dhāraṇī scripture as well as its practitioners."
Before long, he shall attain equal and perfect enlightenment.
At that time, all the Māra kings were filled with joy and leaped for gladness at such an unprecedented occurrence;
they immediately rose from their seats and prostrated themselves at the feet of the Bodhisattva.
Surrounded by those who joyfully received and practiced this dhāraṇī scripture from beginning to end,
Vajraghoṣa then rose from his seat,
joined his palms in reverent salutation, and addressed Puṣpaketu:
Excellent, O assembly of dharmas!
You who are gathered as sages, come bearing this Mahāvaipulya Dhāraṇī to rescue me,
so that my lifespan may increase and the aspiration for the Dharma may arise within me.
Just as one who has died may be born again, so too am I now.
You are now the heroic champion within the Dharma, the mother of all dharmas.
"May I give rise to a firm mind of the Dharma within my body.
Puṣpaketu said, "I am not the mother of these dharmas. Such is the dhāraṇī.
"It can serve as a mother and it can also serve as a father.
You should receive and uphold this dhāraṇī.
At that time, Ghoṣadatta addressed Puṣpakūṭa, saying:
I have often seen the World-Honored One surrounded before and behind by an immeasurable great assembly as he preached the Dharma.
At that time, Puṣpasaṃcaya asked Ghoṣadatta, "What is his name?"
The answer is: He is named Śākyamuni.
His compassion universally covers immeasurable sentient beings without distinction from yours;
his great kindness is likewise immeasurable and even surpasses yours.
"He rescues all from the calamities of the hells and bestows immeasurable happiness.
We two should go there together;
by making offerings to the World-Honored One, we shall surely obtain great benefit."
When these words were spoken,
eighty-two billion devas of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven from within the void performed celestial music, burned incense, and scattered flowers as offerings, forming a great mass of blossoms.
At that time, among the assembly in the void,
there was a celestial king named Mahākarṣa who addressed the host of devas:
"These two Great Beings intend to propagate the Great Dharma."
"We shall go there so that we may correctly hear the nectar of the Buddhas.
Then the two great beings rose from their seats, adjusted their robes, and departed along the road together with the hosts of Māras and the devas and humans.
At that time, the devas immediately followed the two men and went to the Jetavana.
Then, the World-Honored One, hearing the celestial music from afar,
arose from his meditative concentration and addressed Ānanda, saying:
"Go outside and listen to what sound this is.
At that time, Ānanda, having received the World-Honored One’s instruction, immediately went outside to listen.
He saw two men surrounded before and behind by an immeasurable great assembly.
It was as if a mountain of gold had come to the Jetavana.
At that time, Ānanda returned to the Jetavana,
knelt with his palms joined, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
Outside, there were two persons whose bodies were like mountains of gold;
they were subtle and beyond comparison, like the light of the sun,
capable of illuminating all things so that both the internal and external were clearly transparent.
At that time, before Ānanda had finished speaking,
the Bodhisattva Puṣpaketu emitted a great radiance that universally illuminated immeasurable worlds in the ten directions, pervading them all without exception.
All who behold this light are liberated.
At that time, Puṣpacitra silently reflected to himself, "By what shall I bear witness?
Having formed this thought, he—
At that time, Vipaśyin emerged from hell and,
leading ninety-two billion beings among the guilty, followed the light to arrive at the Sahā world.
Likewise, from each of the worlds of the ten directions, ninety-two billion beings among the guilty were led by him in the same manner.
Following the light, they arrived at the Sahā world.
At that time, an immeasurable and boundless multitude,
surrounding them from front and back, reached the Jetavana Grove.
He saw Śākyamuni Buddha,
as well as these two great worthy men standing to the left and right of the Buddha.
At that time, Śāriputra...
Seeing that there were doubts in the minds of this great assembly— specifically, that the five hundred great disciples and the rest of the multitude each harbored their own uncertainties—
Śāriputra, knowing the doubts in the hearts of the assembly and being himself likewise not yet fully enlightened, [addressed them].
He immediately rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder,
knelt with his right knee on the ground, and addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One, from where have such a great assembly as this come?"
Suddenly they arrived here in the Jeta Grove.
Thus did the World-Honored One appear, whom these bodhisattvas had never seen before but now behold;
thus did this celestial being appear, whom they had never seen before but now behold.
Thus the Māra King saw what he had never seen before;
thus the sinful person saw what they had never seen before;
and thus did the Bodhisattva, the devas and humans, the Māras, and the denizens of hell all see one another.
"From which direction have you now suddenly come here?
At that time, the World-Honored One remained silent and did not answer. Then Mañjuśrī said to Śāriputra:
"Noble son, regarding this great assembly, I shall now speak; listen attentively.
This bodhisattva is named Puṣpasaṃcaya, and he has thoroughly mastered skillful means."
Coming from the east, they approached the place where the Buddha was.
These various devas were precisely the devas of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven of this world who had come to the Buddha's presence.
This host of Māras was precisely the host of Māras of this world.
Among these sinners, the foremost is named Bhaṇḍa.
You should now know that before the World-Honored One appeared in the world,
this man committed unwholesome deeds and entered hell, where he underwent suffering for a long time.
Do you not see this Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Puṣpaketu emitting rays of great compassion?
By means of this light, he has been able to emerge from the Avīci Great Hell and come here to this place.
Śāriputra said, "I have long heard the Buddha say that those who commit unwholesome deeds enter hell;
why do you now say that the seer Vāṣpa [has done so]?"
Having emerged from hell, they encounter the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha;
and other sentient beings with various karmic offenses from other directions also come to this place—
how much more so, then, for Vaṅga?
The Buddha has said that a single person performing unwholesome deeds causes many people to fall into hell.
This matter is difficult to believe; what is the meaning of this?
“Mañjuśrī, I pray that you will speak briefly,
so that I may be freed from all my doubts.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
"Excellent, excellent! You have asked well about this matter.
Listen attentively, listen attentively, and I shall explain it for you.
Śāriputra said, "So be it, World-Honored One; we wish and desire to hear it."
The Buddha told Śāriputra,
"Good son, do not speak thus. This great assembly all has its causes and conditions."
Those who come to me briefly comprise three groups.
The first group consists of the inconceivable assembly of bodhisattvas.
It is because they wish me to proclaim the Mahāvaipulya Dhāraṇī and wish me to reveal the unprecedented skillful means that they have come to obscure this Bhikṣu Thunder-Sound.
“I shall now speak of the causes and conditions of the bhikṣu Ghoṣila’s roots of goodness; listen attentively.
Śāriputra said, “So be it, World-Honored One; we wish to hear it with joy.”
Good son, as for the second assembly,
it consists of the Bodhisattva Puṣpaketu and the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven;
this is why they have come to my presence.
It is because they wish to manifest the majestic spiritual power of this dhāraṇī, and also because they wish to proclaim the supernatural powers of the Buddhas of the ten directions;
for these reasons, they have come to my presence.
Good son, as for the third assembly,
because they desire to shatter the fixed retribution of all sentient beings,
these assemblies come to me for this reason.
"Good son, do not speak thus.
The seer Vāma is not a person of hell. Why is this?
Listen attentively now, and you shall understand. Good son, the word 'vā' means 'heaven' (deva)."
"Vijñā" means wisdom;
therefore, it is called "vibhāṣā.
For one who possesses such celestial wisdom, how could there ever be the possibility of ultimately undergoing the sufferings of hell? Such a thing is absolutely impossible.
Furthermore, son of good family, "Bha" means "vast" and "Uṇḍa" means "pervasive.
How could it be that one who is vast and pervasive regarding all dharmas would ultimately enter hell? Such a thing is impossible.
Furthermore, good son, *bha* means "high" and *ṣaṇḍa* means "sublime.
